items.label: History and Analysis of Western Music

items.text: Select six theory courses in consultation with a faculty adviser.

items.label: Performance Organizations
items.notes: Complete two years (12 units) of performance organizations utilizing students’ major instruments, as assigned by the chair or designated faculty member.

nodes.title: Music Theory I
groups: Preparation for the Major: Music Theory
nodes.description: Lecture, four hours. Preparation: passing score on departmental examination. Course 20A is enforced Students must receive grade of C or better to proceed to next course in sequence. Theory: species counterpoint through fifth species; description of triads and inversions. P/NP or letter grading.

nodes.title: Music Theory II
groups: Preparation for the Major: Music Theory
nodes.prereq_text: course 20A with grade of C or better
nodes.description: Lecture, four hours. Theory: diatonic harmony through secondary dominants and diminished sevenths; modulations to dominant and relative keys; writing of four-part chorales; style composition in baroque dance forms; introduction to figured bass notation. P/NP or letter grading.

nodes.title: Music Theory III
groups: Preparation for the Major: Music Theory
nodes.prereq_text: course 20B with grade of C or better
nodes.description: Lecture, four hours. Theory: chromatic harmony including development of tonality, 1800 to 1850; appropriate analysis and style composition. P/NP or letter grading.

nodes.title: Music Theory IV
nodes.prereq_text: course 20C with grade of C (2.0) or better
nodes.description: Lecture, four hours; discussion, four hours. Preparation: passing score on departmental first-year examination. Theory: baroque counterpoint including chorale prelude; two-part invention; exposition and first modulation of three-part invention; canonic principles; analysis of inventions, canons, and fugues. Musicianship: sight-singing of extended chromatic melodies; advanced harmonic dictation (diatonic and chromatic); keyboard harmonization of modulating melodies; elementary score reading. P/NP or letter grading.

nodes.title: Music Theory V
nodes.prereq_text: course 120A with grade of C (2.0) or better
nodes.description: Lecture, four hours; discussion, four hours. Theory: advanced chromatic harmony including development of harmony from 1850; analytical projects; style composition. Musicianship: advanced score reading; advanced harmonic dictation; preparation for departmental examination. P/NP or letter grading.

nodes.title: Music Theory VI
nodes.prereq_text: course 120B with grade of C (2.0) or better
nodes.description: Lecture, four hours; discussion, two hours; listening, two hours. 20th-century harmonic language, including nonfunctional harmony, polytonality, free atonality, serialism, and minimalism. P/NP or letter grading.

nodes.title: History and Analysis of Western Music to 1700
groups: The Major: History and Analysis of Western Music
nodes.prereq_text: course M6C
nodes.description: Lecture, four hours; discussion, one hour. Students must receive grade of C or better to proceed to next course in sequence. Survey of Western music from its beginnings to 1700; examination of representative compositions within their cultural contexts and development of analytical methods appropriate to each repertory. Letter grading.

nodes.title: History and Analysis of Western Music, 1700 to 1800
groups: The Major: History and Analysis of Western Music
nodes.prereq_text: course 140A with grade of C or better
nodes.description: Lecture, four hours; discussion, one hour. Survey of Western music from 1700 to 1890; examination of representative compositions within their cultural contexts and development of analytical methods appropriate to each repertory. Letter grading.

nodes.title: History and Analysis of Western Music, 1890 to Present
groups: The Major: History and Analysis of Western Music
nodes.prereq_text: course 140B with grade of C or better
nodes.description: Lecture, four hours; discussion, one hour. Survey of Western music from 1890 to present; examination of representative compositions within their cultural contexts and development of analytical methods appropriate to each repertory. Letter grading.

nodes.title: Symphonic Band
groups: Preparation for the Major: Performance Organizations
nodes.description: Activity, two hours. Preparation: audition. Group performance of instrumental music scored for band. May be repeated for credit without limitation. P/NP or letter grading.

nodes.title: Marching and Varsity Bands
groups: Preparation for the Major: Performance Organizations
nodes.description: Activity, six hours. Preparation: audition. Group performance of special band arrangements for football and basketball games as well as special events. May be repeated for credit without limitation. P/NP or letter grading.

nodes.title: UCLA Chorale
groups: Preparation for the Major: Performance Organizations
nodes.description: Activity, four hours. Preparation: audition. Large mixed ensemble performing choral music of all periods appropriate for concert choral ensemble. May be repeated for credit without limitation. May be concurrently scheduled with course C480A. P/NP or letter grading.

nodes.title: Chamber Singers
groups: Preparation for the Major: Performance Organizations
nodes.description: Activity, four hours. Preparation: audition. Designed primarily for Music Performance majors. Select mixed ensemble performing chamber choral music of all periods. May be repeated for credit without limitation. May be concurrently scheduled with course C480B. P/NP or letter grading.

nodes.title: Opera Workshop
groups: Preparation for the Major: Performance Organizations
nodes.description: Activity, six hours. Preparation: audition. Rehearsal and performance of scenes and complete operas, as well as repertoire, stage movement, and foreign language diction coaching. May be repeated for credit without limitation. May be concurrently scheduled with course C480C. P/NP or letter grading.

nodes.title: Symphony Orchestra
groups: Preparation for the Major: Performance Organizations
nodes.description: Activity, three hours. Preparation: audition. Group performance of symphonic orchestral literature. May be repeated for credit without limitation. May be concurrently scheduled with course C480D. P/NP or letter grading.

nodes.title: Philharmonia
groups: Preparation for the Major: Performance Organizations
nodes.description: Activity, six hours. Preparation: audition. Designed primarily for Music Performance majors. Group performance of symphonic orchestral literature, as well as orchestral accompaniment for operatic and major choral works. May be repeated for credit without limitation. May be concurrently scheduled with course C480E. P/NP or letter grading.

nodes.title: Wind Ensemble
groups: Preparation for the Major: Performance Organizations
nodes.description: Activity, six hours. Preparation: audition. Group performance of concert literature for wind ensemble. May be repeated for credit without limitation. May be concurrently scheduled with course C480G. P/NP or letter grading.

nodes.title: Piano/Keyboard Accompanying
groups: Preparation for the Major: Performance Organizations
nodes.description: Activity, four hours; outside study, two hours. Collaboration with large ensembles, instrumentalists, and/or vocalists in role of accompanists. Performance includes, but is not limited to, lessons, rehearsals, special studio performance projects, master classes, concerts, auditions, juries, and recitals. May be repeated for maximum of 12 units. Concurrently scheduled with course C484A. P/NP or letter grading.

nodes.title: Guitar Accompanying
groups: Preparation for the Major: Performance Organizations
nodes.description: Activity, four hours; outside study, two hours. Collaboration with instrumentalists and/or vocalists in role of accompanists. Performance includes, but is not limited to, lessons, rehearsals, special studio performance projects, master classes, concerts, auditions, juries, and recitals. May be repeated for credit without limitation. Concurrently scheduled with course C484B. P/NP or letter grading.

nodes.title: Harp Accompanying
groups: Preparation for the Major: Performance Organizations
nodes.description: Activity, four hours; outside study, two hours. Collaboration with instrumentalists and/or vocalists in role of accompanists. May be repeated for credit without limitation. Concurrently scheduled with course C484C. P/NP or letter grading.

nodes.title: Introduction to Global Musicianship
nodes.description: (Same as Ethnomusicology M6A and Musicology M6A.) Laboratory, four hours. Course M6A is enforced Students must receive grade of C– or better to proceed to next course in sequence. Introduction to global musicianship through in-depth exploration of basic musical elements through performance, aural skills, and active listening. Engages with melodic information represented in solfège, harmonic information in Nashville number system, and rhythmic information in both Western notation and digital audio workstation grid visualization. Letter grading.

nodes.title: Introduction to Musicianship
nodes.prereq_text: course M6A with grade of C– or better
nodes.description: (Same as Ethnomusicology M6B and Musicology M6B.) Laboratory, four hours. Preparation: placement examination. Introduction to musicianship through in-depth exploration of basic common musical elements and training in aural recognition, sight singing, dictation, and keyboard skills. Focus on topics such as tonal and modal harmony, rhythm, improvisation, composition, notation, and ear training to prepare students for later theory courses, participation in music ensembles, advanced study in music, and professional careers. Letter grading.

nodes.title: Introduction to Musicianship
nodes.prereq_text: course M6B with grade of C– or better
nodes.description: (Same as Ethnomusicology M6C and Musicology M6C.) Laboratory, four hours. Preparation: placement examination. Introduction to musicianship through in-depth exploration of basic common musical elements and training in aural recognition, sight singing, dictation, and keyboard skills. Focus on topics such as tonal and modal harmony, rhythm, improvisation, composition, notation, and ear training to prepare students for later theory courses, participation in music ensembles, advanced study in music, and professional careers. Letter grading.
